```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Agergaard_2025_tacrolimus"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Agergaard_2025_tacrolimus"))$description`
* Article: [Br J Clin Pharmacol 2025;91(3):761-773](https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.16277)
  (open access, PMC11862786)

The paper links whole-blood and intracellular (peripheral blood mononuclear
cell, PBMC) tacrolimus concentrations in a single population model. The
whole-blood part is a two-compartment model with lagged first-order absorption.
Distribution into PBMCs was found to be instantaneous, so the PBMC concentration
is an algebraic rescaling of the central concentration (Equation 2):

$$C_{PBMC} = R_{C:PBMC} \cdot \frac{A_C}{V_C/F}$$

There is no PBMC compartment and no PBMC rate constant in the final model.

# Population

Agergaard 2025 enrolled 63 stable adult kidney transplant recipients
(>= 3 months after transplantation; median 38 months, IQR 15-79) at three
Danish nephrology departments between June 2021 and October 2023. All took
immediate-release tacrolimus twice daily with mycophenolate, at steady state
(no dose change in the preceding 5 days); the median tacrolimus dose was 2 mg
and a whole-blood trough of 5 ng/mL was generally targeted. Median age was 59
years (IQR 48-68), median weight 86.8 kg, 71.4% were male and 95.2% Caucasian.
Eleven patients (17.5%) were CYP3A5 expressers and 11 (17.5%) were homozygous
for NR1I2 -25385T (rs3814055). Patients were sampled on one occasion, densely
(n = 18; 11 samples over 12 h) or sparsely (n = 45; predose, 0.5, 1.5 and 4 h),
giving 366 whole-blood and 348 PBMC concentrations, all measured by LC-MS/MS
(Methods 2.1, Results 3.1, Table 1).

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Agergaard_2025_tacrolimus")()$population, give.attr = FALSE)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. All
values are the "Final model with covariates" column of Table 2. The PDF encodes
minus signs as control characters, so the signs of the CYP3A5-on-CL/F, female
and lambda rows were read from the rendered table and cross-checked against the
Discussion's percentages.

| Parameter / equation | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL/F, CYP3A5 expresser) | log(28.2) L/h | Table 2, footnote a |
| `e_cyp3a5_nonexpr_cl` | -0.466 | Table 2; Discussion "46.6% lower CL/F" |
| `lvc` (Vc/F, male) | log(180) L | Table 2, footnote b |
| `e_sexf_vc` | -0.345 | Table 2; Discussion "34.5% lower" |
| `lq` (Q/F) | log(51.0) L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvp` (Vp/F) | log(1688) L | Table 2 |
| `lfdepot` (F at 59 years) | fixed(log(1)) | Table 2 footnotes c, d; Results 3.2 |
| `e_age_fdepot` | 0.0123 per year | Table 2; form from Figure 4A (see below) |
| `lmtt` (ka = 1/MTT) | log(0.676) h | Table 2; Results 3.2; Figure 2 |
| `ltlag` | log(0.369) h | Table 2 |
| `lratio_pbmc_central` (R_C:PBMC) | log(1.96) | Table 2, footnote f; Equation 2 |
| `e_cyp3a5_nonexpr_ratio_pbmc_central` | 0.424 | Table 2; Discussion "42.4% higher" |
| `e_nr1i2_hom_ratio_pbmc_central` | 0.607 | Table 2; Discussion "60.7% higher" |
| `e_sample_rbc_contam_ratio_pbmc_central` | 0.709 | Table 2; Results 3.2 "70.9% of R_C:PBMC without redness" |
| `boxcox_lratio_pbmc_central` (lambda) | -2.50 | Table 2 |
| `etalcl` | 0.210^2 | Table 2 IIV 21.0% |
| `etalfdepot` | 0.410^2 | Table 2 IIV 41.0% |
| `etalmtt` | 1.29^2 | Table 2 IIV 129% |
| `etalratio_pbmc_central` | 0.378^2 | Table 2 IIV 37.8%; Results 3.2 (Box-Cox) |
| `propSd` | 0.137 | Table 2 RUV_C 13.7% |
| `propSd_Cpbmc` | 0.354 | Table 2 RUV_PBMC 35.4% |
| Two-compartment ODEs, lag, first-order absorption | n/a | Results 3.2; Methods 2.5; Figure 2 |
| `Cpbmc <- ratio_pbmc_central * Cc` | n/a | Equation 2 |
| Covariate forms (fractional shifts; exponential age) | n/a | Methods 2.6; Table 2; Discussion; Figure 4 |

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Agergaard_2025_tacrolimus")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
# The model must integrate its explicit ODEs, not an auto-detected solved system.
stopifnot(is.null(ui$linCmt) || isFALSE(ui$linCmt))
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)
```

# Simulation helpers

The study population was at steady state on twice-daily dosing. The terminal
half-life implied by Table 2 is long (Vp/F = 1688 L), so the helpers below dose
for 100 intervals and observe the last one. With two declared endpoints (`Cc`
and `Cpbmc`), observation rows nominate the endpoint with `dvid`; both
concentrations are returned as columns on every observation row.

```{r helpers}
tau <- 12
n_dose <- 100
t_last <- (n_dose - 1) * tau
obs_rel <- sort(unique(c(
  0,
  seq(0.30, 3, by = 0.02),
  seq(3.25, tau, by = 0.25)
)))

# One row per subject in `subj` (columns: id plus covariates) -> event table.
make_events <- function(subj, dose_mg = 2) {
  dose <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = (seq_len(n_dose) - 1) * tau) |>
    mutate(amt = dose_mg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = t_last + obs_rel) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dvid, everything())
}

ref_subject <- function(id = 1L, ...) {
  base <- tibble(
    id = id, AGE = 59, SEXF = 0, CYP3A5_EXPR = 1,
    SNP_NR1I2_RS3814055_HOM = 0, SAMPLE_RBC_CONTAM = 0
  )
  mods <- list(...)
  for (nm in names(mods)) base[[nm]] <- mods[[nm]]
  base
}

solve_ss <- function(model, subj, omega = NULL) {
  args <- list(
    model, make_events(subj),
    keep = setdiff(names(subj), "id"), returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  if (!is.null(omega)) args$omega <- omega
  out <- withCallingHandlers(
    as.data.frame(do.call(rxode2::rxSolve, args)),
    # Typical-value solves use zeroRe(), for which this warning is expected.
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
  if (is.null(out$id)) out$id <- subj$id[1]
  out$tad <- out$time - t_last
  out
}

auc_trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
```

# Deterministic structure checks

## Steady-state mass balance

Over a steady-state dosing interval, AUC must equal F * Dose / CL. This checks
the dose route, the bioavailability, the mg-to-ng/mL conversion and that the
ODEs are integrated as written.

```{r mass-balance}
mb <- bind_rows(
  ref_subject(1L),
  ref_subject(2L, CYP3A5_EXPR = 0),
  ref_subject(3L, AGE = 31),
  ref_subject(4L, SEXF = 1)
)
mb_sim <- solve_ss(mod_typ, mb)
mb_tab <- mb_sim |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(
    AGE = first(AGE), SEXF = first(SEXF), CYP3A5_EXPR = first(CYP3A5_EXPR),
    auc_sim = auc_trap(tad, Cc),
    auc_expected = 1000 * 2 * first(fdepot) / first(cl),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc_sim / auc_expected - 1))
knitr::kable(mb_tab, digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(abs(mb_tab$pct_diff) < 0.5))
```

## Covariate relationships: Figure 4

Figure 4 overlays the typical-individual prediction (green dashed line) on the
individual estimates. The maintainers digitised those lines from the published
figure; the packaged model's typical values reproduce every one to within about
1%.

```{r figure4}
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel, ~group, ~digitised, ~model,
  "4B Vc/F (L)", "male", 180.6, 180,
  "4B Vc/F (L)", "female", 118.3, 180 * (1 - 0.345),
  "4C CL/F (L/h)", "CYP3A5 expresser", 28.19, 28.2,
  "4C CL/F (L/h)", "CYP3A5 non-expresser", 15.05, 28.2 * (1 - 0.466),
  "4D R_C:PBMC", "expresser, CC/CT", 1.973, 1.96,
  "4D R_C:PBMC", "expresser, TT", 3.164, 1.96 * 1.607,
  "4D R_C:PBMC", "non-expresser, CC/CT", 2.799, 1.96 * 1.424,
  "4D R_C:PBMC", "non-expresser, TT", 4.507, 1.96 * 1.424 * 1.607
)

# Confirm the "model" column is what the packaged model actually computes.
grid4 <- bind_rows(
  ref_subject(1L), ref_subject(2L, SEXF = 1),
  ref_subject(3L, CYP3A5_EXPR = 0),
  ref_subject(4L, SNP_NR1I2_RS3814055_HOM = 1),
  ref_subject(5L, CYP3A5_EXPR = 0, SNP_NR1I2_RS3814055_HOM = 1)
)
s4 <- solve_ss(mod_typ, grid4) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(vc = first(vc), cl = first(cl), R = first(Cpbmc / Cc), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(s4$vc[1:2], fig4$model[1:2])),
  isTRUE(all.equal(s4$cl[c(1, 3)], fig4$model[3:4])),
  isTRUE(all.equal(s4$R[c(1, 4, 3, 5)], fig4$model[5:8]))
)

fig4 <- fig4 |> mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model / digitised - 1))
fig4 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Figure panel" = panel, "Group" = group, "Digitised" = digitised,
    "Model" = model, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(abs(fig4$pct_diff) < 2))
```

## Functional form of the age effect on F

Table 2 gives the age coefficient (0.0123) but not the functional form; Methods
2.6 says continuous covariates were normalised to the median and tested as
linear, exponential and power functions. The typical-individual line of
Figure 4A, digitised below, separates the three readings.

```{r age-form}
fig4a <- tibble::tribble(
  ~AGE, ~F_digitised,
  21, 0.628,
  31, 0.710,
  59, 1.000,
  75, 1.214,
  81, 1.302
)
age_forms <- fig4a |>
  mutate(
    exponential = exp(0.0123 * (AGE - 59)),
    linear = 1 + 0.0123 * (AGE - 59),
    power = (AGE / 59)^0.0123
  )
knitr::kable(age_forms, digits = 3)
rms <- function(x) sqrt(mean(x^2))
age_rms <- c(
  exponential = rms(age_forms$exponential - age_forms$F_digitised),
  linear = rms(age_forms$linear - age_forms$F_digitised),
  power = rms(age_forms$power - age_forms$F_digitised)
)
age_rms
stopifnot(
  age_rms[["exponential"]] < 0.01,
  age_rms[["linear"]] > 3 * age_rms[["exponential"]],
  age_rms[["power"]] > 3 * age_rms[["exponential"]]
)

# The packaged model uses the exponential form.
s_age <- solve_ss(mod_typ, tibble(
  id = 1:5, AGE = fig4a$AGE, SEXF = 0, CYP3A5_EXPR = 1,
  SNP_NR1I2_RS3814055_HOM = 0, SAMPLE_RBC_CONTAM = 0
)) |>
  distinct(id, fdepot)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(s_age$fdepot, age_forms$exponential)))
```

The exponential form matches the digitised line almost exactly (a free
exponential fit to the line recovers 0.0123 per year with F = 1.000 at 59
years). The linear form is off by about 0.09 at 21 years, and the median-ratio
power form is nearly flat.

# Covariate profiles: Figure 5

Figure 5 shows steady-state whole-blood and PBMC profiles for pairs of
covariate values. The paper does not state the dose or the values of the
covariates that were held fixed. The profiles below are typical-value
predictions at 2 mg twice daily (the Table 1 median dose) for a 59-year-old
male CYP3A5 expresser carrying a NR1I2 -25385 C allele unless the panel varies
that covariate.

```{r figure5, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9}
f5_groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel, ~label, ~AGE, ~SEXF, ~CYP3A5_EXPR, ~SNP_NR1I2_RS3814055_HOM,
  "A Sex", "Man", 59, 0, 1, 0,
  "A Sex", "Woman", 59, 1, 1, 0,
  "B Age", "31 years", 31, 0, 1, 0,
  "B Age", "75 years", 75, 0, 1, 0,
  "C NR1I2-25385C>T", "CC or CT", 59, 0, 1, 0,
  "C NR1I2-25385C>T", "TT", 59, 0, 1, 1,
  "D CYP3A5", "Expresser", 59, 0, 1, 0,
  "D CYP3A5", "Non-expresser", 59, 0, 0, 0,
  "E Extremes", "75 y man, TT, non-expresser", 75, 0, 0, 1,
  "E Extremes", "31 y woman, CC/CT, expresser", 31, 1, 1, 0
) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()), SAMPLE_RBC_CONTAM = 0)

f5_sim <- solve_ss(
  mod_typ,
  select(f5_groups, id, AGE, SEXF, CYP3A5_EXPR, SNP_NR1I2_RS3814055_HOM, SAMPLE_RBC_CONTAM)
) |>
  left_join(select(f5_groups, id, panel, label), by = "id")

f5_sim |>
  select(panel, label, tad, `Whole blood` = Cc, PBMC = Cpbmc) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`Whole blood`, PBMC), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(matrix = factor(matrix, c("Whole blood", "PBMC"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, conc, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(panel ~ matrix, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Typical concentration (model units)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the layout of Figure 5 of Agergaard 2025 (typical values, 2 mg b.i.d.)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))

f5_tab <- f5_sim |>
  group_by(panel, label) |>
  summarise(
    auc_wb = auc_trap(tad, Cc),
    cmax_wb = max(Cc),
    ctrough_wb = last(Cc),
    ratio_pbmc = first(Cpbmc / Cc),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
f5_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Panel" = panel, "Group" = label, "Whole-blood AUC0-12 (ng*h/mL)" = auc_wb,
    "Whole-blood Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax_wb, "Whole-blood trough (ng/mL)" = ctrough_wb,
    "Cpbmc / Cc" = ratio_pbmc
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

f5v <- function(lab, col) f5_tab[[col]][f5_tab$label == lab]
stopifnot(
  # Sex acts on Vc/F only: same exposure, sharper peak in women.
  abs(f5v("Woman", "auc_wb") / f5v("Man", "auc_wb") - 1) < 0.005,
  f5v("Woman", "cmax_wb") > f5v("Man", "cmax_wb"),
  # Age acts on F: exposure scales by exp(0.0123 * 44).
  abs(f5v("75 years", "auc_wb") / f5v("31 years", "auc_wb") / exp(0.0123 * 44) - 1) < 0.005,
  # NR1I2 acts on R only.
  abs(f5v("TT", "auc_wb") / f5v("CC or CT", "auc_wb") - 1) < 0.005,
  abs(f5v("TT", "ratio_pbmc") - 1.96 * 1.607) < 1e-6,
  # CYP3A5 acts on CL/F and R.
  abs(f5v("Non-expresser", "auc_wb") / f5v("Expresser", "auc_wb") - 1 / (1 - 0.466)) < 0.01,
  abs(f5v("Non-expresser", "ratio_pbmc") - 1.96 * 1.424) < 1e-6
)
```

Three features of Figure 5 are reproduced: the NR1I2 genotype moves only the
PBMC profile (panel C); the CYP3A5 non-expresser has about 1.9-fold higher
whole-blood exposure and a further 1.42-fold higher PBMC:blood ratio (panel D);
and in every panel the plotted PBMC curve sits at R_C:PBMC times the
whole-blood curve, with the PBMC axis numerically on the whole-blood scale. Two
panels of the published figure cannot be reproduced from Table 2; see
"Assumptions and deviations".

# Virtual cohort

The cohort below approximates Table 1. Patient-level data are not public. Age
is drawn from a normal distribution matching the median and IQR (59, 48-68
years; values outside the 18-85-year eligibility band are redrawn, not
clamped); sex, CYP3A5 status and NR1I2 -25385 TT status are drawn independently
at the Table 1 frequencies. All PBMC samples are taken as uncontaminated
(`SAMPLE_RBC_CONTAM = 0`). The study titrated doses to a trough target, so a
single 2 mg twice-daily dose for everyone (the Table 1 median) overstates the
spread of exposures relative to the observed data.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20250301)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250301)

draw_age <- function(n, median = 59, sd = 20 / 1.349, lo = 18, hi = 85) {
  out <- rnorm(n, median, sd)
  bad <- out < lo | out > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    out[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), median, sd)
    bad <- out < lo | out > hi
  }
  out
}

n_sub <- 200
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  AGE = draw_age(n_sub),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 18 / 63),
  CYP3A5_EXPR = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 11 / 63),
  SNP_NR1I2_RS3814055_HOM = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 11 / 63),
  SAMPLE_RBC_CONTAM = 0
)
summary(cohort[, -1])
```

# Simulation and comparison with Figure 3

```{r vpc, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
sim <- solve_ss(mod, cohort) |>
  mutate(cyp3a5 = ifelse(CYP3A5_EXPR == 1, "Expresser", "Non-expresser"))

vpc <- sim |>
  select(id, tad, `Whole blood (ng/mL)` = Cc, `PBMC (model units)` = Cpbmc) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(id, tad), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(matrix, tad) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(conc, 0.10), p50 = median(conc), p90 = quantile(conc, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(tad)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.25, fill = "seagreen") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~matrix, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Concentration",
    caption = "Compare with Figure 3A,B of Agergaard 2025 (median and 10th-90th percentiles)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

wb_med <- vpc |> filter(matrix == "Whole blood (ng/mL)")
wb_trough <- wb_med$p50[wb_med$tad == max(wb_med$tad)]
wb_peak <- max(wb_med$p50)
pb_med <- vpc |> filter(matrix == "PBMC (model units)")

# Approximate medians read from Figure 3A,B (prediction-corrected observed data).
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~matrix, ~point, ~observed,
  "Whole blood (ng/mL)", "predose / 12 h", 6,
  "Whole blood (ng/mL)", "peak", 12,
  "PBMC (pg/10^6 cells)", "predose / 12 h", 40,
  "PBMC (pg/10^6 cells)", "peak", 95
) |>
  mutate(simulated = c(wb_trough, wb_peak, last(pb_med$p50), max(pb_med$p50))) |>
  mutate(observed_over_simulated = observed / simulated)
fig3 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Matrix" = matrix, "Time" = point, "Observed median (Figure 3)" = observed,
    "Simulated median" = simulated, "Observed / simulated" = observed_over_simulated
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(wb_trough > 3, wb_trough < 12, wb_peak > 1.5 * wb_trough)
```

The observed whole-blood median in Figure 3A runs from about 6 ng/mL predose
to about 12 ng/mL at 1.5-2 h. The simulated median follows the same course,
slightly higher because every virtual patient takes 2 mg rather than a
trough-titrated dose. The observed PBMC data in Figure 3B are plotted in
pg/10^6 cells and sit two- to three-fold above the simulated `Cpbmc`; see
"Assumptions and deviations" for why the PBMC absolute scale cannot be
reproduced from the published information.

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA, so PKNCA is used to summarise the simulated
steady-state interval by CYP3A5 group and to check it against the
closed-form identity AUC0-tau = F * Dose / CL for each subject.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, cyp3a5, tad, Cc, Cpbmc)
nca_dose <- sim |>
  distinct(id, cyp3a5) |>
  mutate(tad = 0, amt = 2)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = tau,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)

run_nca <- function(conc_col) {
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
    dplyr::rename(nca_conc, conc = all_of(conc_col)),
    conc ~ tad | cyp3a5 + id
  )
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ tad | cyp3a5 + id)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}
nca_wb <- run_nca("Cc")
nca_pbmc <- run_nca("Cpbmc")

summ <- function(res, matrix) {
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "cmin", "auclast")) |>
    group_by(cyp3a5, PPTESTCD) |>
    summarise(
      value = sprintf(
        "%.3g [%.3g-%.3g]", median(PPORRES),
        quantile(PPORRES, 0.05), quantile(PPORRES, 0.95)
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = value) |>
    mutate(matrix = matrix, .before = 1)
}
bind_rows(summ(nca_wb, "Whole blood"), summ(nca_pbmc, "PBMC")) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Matrix" = matrix, "CYP3A5" = cyp3a5, "Cmax" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "Cmin" = cmin, "AUC0-12" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated steady-state NCA, median [5th-95th percentile]; 2 mg b.i.d.")

auc_check <- as.data.frame(nca_wb) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, auc_nca = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(distinct(sim, id, cl, fdepot), by = "id") |>
  mutate(auc_expected = 1000 * 2 * fdepot / cl, pct_diff = 100 * (auc_nca / auc_expected - 1))
summary(auc_check$pct_diff)
stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_check) == n_sub,
  abs(median(auc_check$pct_diff)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(auc_check$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5
)
```

# Sensitivity to the reading of "IIV (%)"

Table 2 headlines its random-effect column "IIV (%)" without saying whether the
figure is 100 times the standard deviation of the eta or an arithmetic
coefficient of variation. The packaged model uses the eta-SD reading
(variance = (IIV/100)^2), because the same column reports 37.8% for the
Box-Cox-transformed R_C:PBMC eta, for which the log-normal CV identity does not
apply. The alternative reading, omega^2 = log(1 + (IIV/100)^2), is simulated
below. It changes the MTT variance materially (1.66 vs 0.98) and the other
three by under 8%.

```{r omega-sensitivity}
iiv_pct <- c(etalcl = 21.0, etalfdepot = 41.0, etalmtt = 129, etalratio_pbmc_central = 37.8)
om_sd <- (iiv_pct / 100)^2
om_cv <- log(1 + (iiv_pct / 100)^2)

shipped <- diag(ui$omega)[names(iiv_pct)]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(shipped), unname(om_sd))))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    eta = names(iiv_pct), `IIV (%)` = iiv_pct,
    `variance, eta-SD reading (shipped)` = om_sd,
    `variance, CV reading` = om_cv, check.names = FALSE
  ),
  digits = 4, row.names = FALSE
)

# Same model, with only the four variances replaced by the CV reading.
om_cv_mat <- ui$omega
for (nm in names(om_cv)) om_cv_mat[nm, nm] <- om_cv[[nm]]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(diag(om_cv_mat)[names(iiv_pct)]), unname(om_cv))))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250302)
sim_cv <- solve_ss(mod, cohort, omega = om_cv_mat)

sens <- bind_rows(
  sim |> mutate(reading = "eta SD (shipped)"),
  sim_cv |> mutate(reading = "arithmetic CV")
) |>
  group_by(reading, id) |>
  summarise(
    cmax = max(Cc), tmax = tad[which.max(Cc)], auc = auc_trap(tad, Cc),
    ctrough = last(Cc), .groups = "drop"
  )
sens_tab <- sens |>
  pivot_longer(c(cmax, tmax, auc, ctrough), names_to = "metric") |>
  group_by(reading, metric) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(value), p05 = quantile(value, 0.05), p95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
sens_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Reading" = reading, "Whole-blood metric" = metric, "Median" = median, "5th pct" = p05, "95th pct" = p95) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

med <- function(r, m) sens_tab$median[sens_tab$reading == r & sens_tab$metric == m]
auc_ratio <- med("arithmetic CV", "auc") / med("eta SD (shipped)", "auc")
auc_ratio
stopifnot(auc_ratio > 0.85, auc_ratio < 1.15)
```

As expected, steady-state exposure barely depends on the reading, because AUC
does not depend on MTT and the CL/F and F variances differ little. The reading
matters mainly for the spread of Tmax and of the peak concentration.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Absorption.** Results 3.2 describes "first-order absorption ... with an
  absorption lag-time", Figure 2 draws a single arrow labelled MTT from the
  dosing compartment to the central compartment, and Table 2 reports no number
  of transit compartments. The model therefore uses ka = 1/MTT with the IIV on
  MTT.
* **Age on F.** The functional form is not printed. The exponential form,
  centred by subtraction at the median age of 59 years, is the only one that
  reproduces Figure 4A (see above).
* **Box-Cox form.** The paper states that the R_C:PBMC eta was Box-Cox
  transformed with lambda = -2.50 but does not print the equation. The usual
  NONMEM form, eta_tr = (exp(eta)^lambda - 1) / lambda, is used; with a
  negative lambda it gives a long lower tail of R_C:PBMC, consistent with the
  low individual estimates in Figure 4D.
* **IIV scale.** "IIV (%)" is read as 100 times the eta standard deviation; the
  alternative reading is simulated above.
* **Erythrocyte dilution is a direct multiplier.** Results 3.2 and Table 2
  (0.709) agree that contaminated samples had 70.9% of the uncontaminated
  ratio. The Discussion's "R_C:PBMC was 70.8% lower in the samples that were
  contaminated" contradicts both and is not used.
* **PBMC concentration scale.** Table 2 declares R_C:PBMC dimensionless and
  Equation 2 gives the PBMC concentration on the whole-blood scale, which is
  what the packaged model computes and what Figure 5 plots. The observed PBMC
  concentrations in Figures 1 and 3B are plotted in pg/10^6 cells and their
  median runs six- to eight-fold above the whole-blood median in ng/mL
  (Figure 3), against an estimated ratio of about 2-3. Methods 2.2 converts cell-associated amounts to a
  concentration using the mean corpuscular volume of PBMCs from a cited
  reference, but that volume is not reported, so the conversion between the
  model's `Cpbmc` and the plotted pg/10^6 cells cannot be reconstructed. Use
  `Cpbmc` for the ratio-based comparisons the model supports (relative changes
  across covariates, PBMC:blood ratios), not as an absolute intracellular
  concentration.
* **Figure 5A (sex).** The published panel shows the female profile below the
  male one across the whole interval. Sex acts only on Vc/F in Table 2, so the
  steady-state AUC is the same for both sexes and the female peak is higher, as
  the packaged model shows. The figure is not reproducible from Table 2 and the
  table is followed.
* **Figure 5B and E (age).** The published Figure 5B shows identical profiles
  for 31- and 75-year-olds, and the Discussion concludes that age "appears to
  have little bearing". With the Table 2 age effect, the 75-year-old's exposure
  is exp(0.0123 * 44) = 1.72-fold higher. In panel E the published whole-blood
  ratio between the extreme groups is about 2, close to the CYP3A5 effect alone
  (1.87) rather than the 3.2-fold that CYP3A5 and age together give. The age
  effect appears to have been left out of the Figure 5 simulations. Table 2
  (estimate 0.0123, RSE 25.8%, dOFV -8.78 in Supporting Table S1) and Figure 4A
  agree with each other, so the age effect is kept.
* **Figure 5 dose.** The dose behind Figure 5 is not stated (its whole-blood
  concentrations are well below those observed). The replication above uses
  2 mg twice daily and compares ratios rather than absolute levels.
* **Covariates held at the reference.** Haematocrit, albumin, lean body
  weight, ABCB1, CYP3A4*22, NR1I2 -24381A>T, ALT, bilirubin, time since
  transplantation and interacting co-medication were screened and not retained
  (Methods 2.6, Results 3.3). They are documented in the model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded` list.
* **Virtual cohort.** Age, sex and genotypes are drawn independently from the
  Table 1 marginal distributions with a fixed 2 mg twice-daily dose; the
  study's doses were individualised by therapeutic drug monitoring.
